transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-23
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (BrightFind Head of Search), Diego Ruiz (BrightFind ML Eng), Karen Li (BrightFind CTO)

Summary: quick hosted API demo focusing on embeddings and rerank endpoints. Walked through a sample search flow: embed user query -> vector DB retrieval -> rerank with Redwood rerank endpoint. Discussed perf numbers, integration patterns, and security.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about 45 minutes, i'll hand off to samira to do the deep dive and i'll jump in for pricing and customer questions
00:18 Samira: cool thanks jordan, hi maya diego karen, i'm samira, senior solutions engineer at redwood, we'll show the hosted embeddings and rerank endpoints and a quick console walkthrough, okay so first slide — high level flow, you call our embeddings endpoint, we return a vector, you store in your vector db, then for retrieval you can do kNN or hybrid and optionally call our rerank endpoint to rescore top-k with context
00:46 Maya: quick question, when you say rerank, that's a separate api call after retrieval? or is it combined?
:58 Samira: good question — it's a second call typically, you send the top N documents plus the query, we score them and return ranks or scores, that lets you keep the vector DB fast and do a small LLM cost on only the top candidates
01:20 Diego: what's the expected latency on rerank? 95th perc?
01:30 Samira: for hosted we typically see rerank latencies in the 60-250ms range depending on model and prompt length — smaller models are sub-100ms for short contexts, larger models or long doc contexts push higher, we can pin models or pick faster quantized variants to hit targets
01:52 Jordan: to add, our Optimize tooling will recommend model variants and batching settings based on your QPS and tail latency targets, so we try to tune to your 95th pct aim
02:10 Karen: our SLAs want p95 under 200ms for interactive search — is that realistic with hosted?
02:22 Samira: yes many customers hit that — you'll want to keep rerank context short (top 10, trimmed passages), use our smaller rerank model, and enable our KV prefix caching to reuse embeddings for repeated queries, that reduces end-to-end time
02:44 Maya: we're using Pinecone today for storage, any preferred adapters?
02:52 Samira: we have example integrations for Pinecone, Milvus, RedisVector, and Elastic vectors — generally you call embeddings -> upsert to Pinecone and then do kNN and pass top-k to rerank; we can share a sample repo with code snippets
03:20 Diego: how about embedding dim and distance metric? cosine vs euclid — our current infra uses 1536 dims with cosine
03:32 Samira: that's standard, our embeddings endpoint returns 1536 for the model we demoed, we also support 1024/768 dims depending on model selection, and you can normalize for cosine on client side, most vector DBs support either metric
03:50 Jordan: cost note — embeddings are billed per-embedding unit, rerank billed per-token on request and response; Optimize helps estimate unit economics and can simulate costs for your traffic
04:10 Maya: data residency, we need EU-only processing for a subset of user data — can hosted do region pinning?
04:22 Samira: yes, we offer region routing for hosted requests and Private for stricter on-prem requirements; for hosted we can route EU traffic to our EU region, and for enterprise we also support VPC/private deployments with customer-managed network
04:44 Karen: security — we need SOC2, audit logs, KMS for keys, and SSO integration
04:52 Samira: we have SOC2, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs in Console, and KMS integrations; i'll share the security whitepaper, and jordan can get you the SOC2 cert link
05:10 Jordan: quick console demo next — i'll share my screen and show the embeddings request and rerank request in the api explorer, also the per-route latency dashboard
05:28 Jordan: okay sharing, first the api explorer: POST /v1/embeddings, body — model: redwood-text-emb-1, input: your text. here's a python snippet, return is vector float array and metadata id
05:48 Jordan: then for rerank POST /v1/rerank, body model: redwood-rerank-1, query: "user query", candidates: [ {id, text, meta}, ... ] and you get scores and ranked order back, you can choose to return top-1 or scores for reweighting in your scoring pipeline
06:10 Maya: are there example prompts/templates for reranking? we care about fairness and not promoting certain documents by accident
06:20 Samira: yes we maintain prompt templates and also a safety/classifier pre-filter; for rerank we recommend neutral framing and include system instruction to prefer recency or relevance depending on your metric, we can share best-practices doc
06:42 Diego: can rerank use embeddings as side features or just raw text?
06:48 Samira: you can pass embedding similarities as metadata and include them in the rerank prompt; many customers pass score and let the model combine semantic score + BM25 rank for final ordering
07:10 Jordan: let's talk throughput — what's your QPS and typical query budget?
07:18 Maya: today peak 120 qps for search, average 40 qps — p95 matters for UX, cost is secondary but still a factor
07:30 Samira: with 120 qps you'll want to use batching for embeddings (if doing many writes) and continuous batching for rerank if you can tolerate a few ms, also consider using caching for hot queries; Redwood Dedicated can give predictable throughput if you want guaranteed capacity but hosted typically works for this profile too
08:00 Diego: about caching, is prefix/KV cache automatic or client-managed?
08:08 Samira: runtime-level KV prefix caching is automatic for repeated prefixes, you can also set TTLs, it lowers token usage on reranks when context repeats, and Optimize will estimate hit rates based on your traffic pattern
08:30 Maya: integration timeline — if we wanted to run a POC, what's involved?
08:36 Jordan: typical POC is 2-4 weeks: week 0 kickoff and data handshake, week 1 integration and baseline runs, week 2 tuning and rerank prompt iterations, final week validation and cost estimates. we'll provide trial tokens and a POC checklist
09:00 Karen: what about data retention and deletion? compliance requires deletion on request
09:10 Samira: hosted has retention controls and delete APIs, plus audit logs; for stricter policies we recommend Private deployment or dedicated tenancy where you manage storage
09:28 Diego: cross talk, are there examples of rerank prompt that reduce hallucination?
09:34 Samira: yes we include grounding instructions and source quoting where the rerank model should prefer documents that contain the explicit answer indicators, also we truncate nonrelevant sections to reduce noise
09:50 Jordan: competitor note, some teams use OpenAI + Pinecone; we differentiate on latency controls, observability, and cost tooling for serving at scale
10:12 Maya: can we run an A/B with our current pipeline?
10:18 Samira: yes our rollouts support canary and A/B; you can split traffic by route and compare relevance metrics, and Console shows token/cost delta per route
10:40 Diego: curious about model sizes for rerank — what's the tradeoff?
10:46 Samira: larger models give better understanding for longer context but cost more and have higher latency; smaller rerank-specific distilled models often hit sweet spot for semantic ordering, Optimize will nudge models based on your eval set
11:05 Jordan: speaking of evals, bring us your relevance judgments or a small gold set and we can run relevance evals to pick model+prompt combo, we have tooling to compute MRR, NDCG etc
11:24 Maya: we use MRR and Click-through as primary metrics, happy to share sample labels
11:32 Samira: perfect, we'll use that for POC success criteria — target improvements and latency thresholds
11:48 Karen: are there limits on candidate size? like top-k > 100 is expensive?
11:54 Samira: practically we recommend top-k 10-50 for rerank; beyond that costs rise and latency increases, better to pre-filter by BM25 then rerank top 50
12:10 Diego: what's the billing cadence for embeddings/upserts to vector db vs runtime rerank calls?
12:18 Jordan: embeddings billed per embedding call; rerank billed per token; upserts to vector DB are your DB cost — we show unit economics in Console so you can simulate monthly spend
12:40 Maya: any rate limits or bursting?
12:44 Samira: hosted has rate limits but offer burst windows; for production at 120 qps we often recommend Dedicated to avoid throttling and get predictable latencies, or a reserved plan if you want hosted but with capacity commit
13:05 Jordan: quick demo of Console metrics — here we have per-route latency heatmap, token cost breakdown, and model rollout controls where you can canary a new rerank model
13:30 Jordan: i'll paste a sample curl for embeddings and rerank into the chat after the call
13:40 Maya: excellent — on security docs, we'll need SOC2 and KMS integration details before legal signs off
13:48 Jordan: noted, samira will share security packet, and i'll attach our SOC2 link and a sample DPA
14:00 Samira: any other technical questions?
14:06 Diego: curious about compatibility with our java stack and async handlers
14:12 Samira: we have SDKs and HTTP examples for java/python/node, and async patterns are supported with streaming and chunked responses, rerank returns compact json so it should be easy to integrate
14:30 Maya: what success metrics should we track during the POC?
14:36 Jordan: primary: MRR improvement over baseline, secondary: p95 latency under 200ms, tertiary: cost per query within your budget — we'll help define thresholds
14:58 Karen: timeline wise, legal wants the security docs by friday, that's 2026-11-27 for our team to review before kickoff
15:08 Jordan: we'll target sending docs by 2026-11-24 so you have time, and pricing by 11-25, samira will set up POC kickoff for week of 11-30 once data is uploaded
15:28 Maya: cool, thanks everyone
15:34 Jordan: thanks all, i'll follow up with the deck, security packet, trial keys, and the POC checklist, talk soon

End of transcript
